messages.content: What is the freezing point point of water at a pressure of 10 kPa?

function.name: thermodynamics_calculate_boiling_point

message.content:
At a pressure of **10 kPa** (about one‑tenth of an atmosphere), pure water freezes at roughly **–20 °C**.  

This follows the well‑known negative slope of the ice–water equilibrium line on the phase diagram: as pressure decreases below the normal atmospheric value, the melting/freezing temperature drops. At 10 kPa the equilibrium temperature is close to –20 °C (the exact value depends slightly on impurities and measurement precision, but it’s in the –18 °C to –22 °C range).
